terms.meaning: a group of jobs processed together in one run

sections.name: File setup, Tab
sections.title: Setup and the two mode names
sections.what: Marks the page as browser code, imports its parts, and defines two mode names, scan and paste.
sections.why: Likely reason: the two names match two ways of adding jobs. This is inferred from the names only.
sections.watch_out: The mode names are compared as plain text, so a typo in one place makes that mode fail quietly.

sections.name: BatchPage (part 1)
sections.title: Batch page state and scan query setup
sections.what: Holds the page's memory: the current batch, whether a batch is running, error text, the scan query and regions, and scan results. Before a scan, it builds role keywords from the profile and exclusion words based on years of experience and headline, so seniority levels that do not fit are filtered out.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the scan rank results for the user's level without asking them to type filters.
sections.watch_out: The exclusion rules are rough guesses from years and headline words, so an unusual profile can get the wrong filters.

sections.name: BatchPage (part 2)
sections.title: Scan request and starting a batch from results
sections.what: Sends the query, regions, enabled target companies and provider keys to the scan route, then shows the jobs found, all selected. If nothing comes back, it shows one of two messages: jobs were found but none scored high enough, or no jobs were found, with a hint to add a job search key. Starting a batch turns the selected jobs into batch inputs, using the company name from the result or a name guessed from the web address.
sections.why: Likely reason: the scan can return many jobs, so selection happens before any costly evaluation.
sections.watch_out: When the company name is missing it is guessed from the web address, and the job text is only a title and short snippet, which can make evaluations weaker than pasted descriptions.

sections.name: BatchPage (part 3)
sections.title: Pasted job list parsing and page tabs
sections.what: Splits pasted text into jobs at blank lines. The first line of each block is read as company, role and location separated by vertical bars, and the rest is the job text. Also builds the page header with the scan and paste tab buttons, and counts batch items by status.
sections.why: Likely reason: a simple text format lets users paste many jobs at once without filling in a form.
sections.watch_out: A missing vertical bar in the first line puts text in the wrong field, and missing parts silently become Unknown.

sections.name: BatchPage (part 4)
sections.title: Scan tab with results list
sections.what: Shows the query box, region buttons, scan and edit companies buttons, and a note on how scanning works. When results exist, lists them with checkboxes, relevance score, company or web address, location, source and a short snippet. Also offers all, none and evaluate buttons.
sections.why: Likely reason: the user chooses which results to evaluate, since each one takes time and AI use.
sections.watch_out: The note states a cut-off of 20 out of 100, but that number is written as text here, so it can drift from the code that actually filters jobs.

sections.name: BatchPage (part 5)
sections.title: Paste tab and batch progress panel
sections.what: On the paste tab, shows instructions and a large text box for pasted jobs. The evaluate button is disabled while running or when the box is empty. Below, shows any error message, then a panel for the current batch with its id, a running or done label, counts of done, scoring, queued and failed items, and a clear button once it finishes.
sections.why: Likely reason: the counts give live feedback during a long run.
sections.watch_out: The clear button only appears after the batch finishes, so a batch that never finishes cannot be cleared from this page.

sections.name: BatchPage (part 6)
sections.title: Per-job status rows and view links
sections.what: Lists each job in the current batch with company, role, location, a status tag, and a score once done. Scores are green at 4 or above and amber at 3.5 or above. Jobs that have an application record get a view link to their detail page.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user see which evaluations are ready and open them quickly.
sections.watch_out: The view link is built from an internal slug, so changing how slugs are made would break these links.

sections.name: inputStyle
sections.title: Shared input box style
sections.what: Defines one visual style, full width with a dark background and monospace text, used by the input and text box on this page.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the input boxes looking consistent in one place.

summary: The batch intake screen for running the job pipeline over several postings at once. Only its setup was reviewed, so the rest of its behavior is unknown.
purpose: Likely reason: lets the user process many jobs in one run instead of one at a time.
why: Likely reason: adding jobs one by one is slow. The code does not state this.
how: Imports the batch runner, company target lists, default role buckets, the profile, and integration settings. The steps the page takes after that were not reviewed.
inputs: The profile, default buckets, company targets, integration settings, and any saved batch state.
risks: Behavior is unknown because only the imports and a type were reviewed.
debug: Start with the batch runner file, since this page mostly wires it up. If a run seems stuck, check the saved batch state.
